observations: Blue and silver power drill in a blue plastic carrying case.
The brand 'BOSCH' is printed in red on the side of the tool housing.
A 'Professional' label is visible on the side, but the model number below it is blurred and unreadable.
An auxiliary handle and a metal depth stop rod are attached to the front.
The power cord is black and coiled inside the case.
The tool appears to be in very clean, possibly unused condition.
A red selector switch is visible on top of the silver gear housing, suggesting a multi-speed gearbox.
The chuck appears to be a keyed type based on the visible gear teeth.

claims.evidence: The Bosch logo is clearly visible on the tool in photo 0.
The rating plate showing the wattage is not visible in the photo.
The country of origin is typically found on the rating plate, which is not shown.
While it belongs to the 'Professional' line, 'heavy duty' is a performance claim that cannot be verified remotely without testing.

risks.proof: A clear, high-resolution photo of the rating plate showing the serial number and manufacturing details.
A video of the drill running through its speed settings and impact modes.
A photo of the rating plate showing the technical specifications (W).

proof_requests: Photo of the rating plate (the sticker with technical specs and serial number).
Video of the drill running and switching between gears.
response.reason: The specific model number and the 1300W power rating are unreadable in the photo. Because Bosch tools are frequently counterfeited and the price varies significantly between models, the rating plate must be seen to confirm identity and authenticity.
